newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee exporters to discuss ACPC with gov't.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee exporters to discuss ACPC with gov't.

text.p: Officials from Brazil's Coffee Exporters' Federation (Febec) will discuss Brazil's export performance within an agreement amongst producer nations with a top government official on April 24, the Febec head said.

"We are going to discuss what we expect is going to be our performance between now and the end of the semester and what should be our strategy in the new coffee year," said Febec president Oswaldo Aranha.

Febec representatives will first hold an internal meeting at 1430 local/1530 GMT to be followed by talks at 1700 local/2000 GMT with Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
Under a plan by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) which runs until the end of June this year, Brazil is to export no more than six million 60-kg bags between January and June.
However traders are already speculating that, based on export registrations, the country may export significantly more than this, possibly even up to seven million bags.
In the first quarter of this year, Brazil shipped 3.89 million bags according to Febec statistics.
Based on export registrations as of April 11, a further 2.66 million bags could be shipped in the second quarter, giving already a possible total of 6.55 million bags.

However actual shipments of coffee so far this month have been much slower than expected, with bills of lading covering 403,794 bags received by April 18 against 770,900 bags by the same period the previous month.
Moreover while April export registrations as of April 11 were for 1.64 million bags, certificates of origin had been issued for only 953,161 bags as of last Friday.
In April to June last year, Brazil shipped 1.99 million bags using the drought hit 1995/96 crop and some early sales of the 1996/97 harvest.
In April to June 1995 when exporters had access to a similar-sized crop as this year, shipments in the same three months were 3.37 million bags.
As well as assessing the near-term prospects, exporters will discuss Brazil's position on any further market mechanisms from July 1997 within the context of the ACPC, Aranha said.
This will involve deciding whether exporters would back the idea of continued market controls and if so, what should be Brazil's export allowance under any new plan, he added.
